question: What is open information extraction and how is it used to build a knowledge graph?

frames.data: data: {"type":"block","block":{"type":"CitedSummary","id":"turn-1b7765d60077","meta":{"status":"ready","error":null},"data":{"segments":[{"text":"Open information extraction (OpenIE) is a schemaless process of extracting knowledge graph triples from text. An LLM can be used to do this.","citationIds":["c1"]},{"text":"In the EDC framework, it is the first phase. It freely extracts a list of entity-relation triplets from the input text, without a predefined schema.","citationIds":["c2"]},{"text":"A knowledge graph is built from these triplets. A triplet is the basic unit of a KG and consists of a subject, a predicate, and an object. Entities and relations become nodes and edges.","citationIds":["c3","c4"]},{"text":"Open extraction can leave the schema redundant. EDC therefore follows it with schema definition and canonicalization. These steps standardize the triplets so that semantically equivalent entity and relation types share the same phrase.
